n1.vektorer-och-skalarprodukt.2: A vector is a list of numbers. In the model every token is a vector of 4096 numbers, and such a vector can be seen as an arrow in a room with 4096 dimensions.
n1.vektorer-och-skalarprodukt.3: The dot product multiplies two vectors element by element and sums:
n1.vektorer-och-skalarprodukt.4: a · b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + … + a_d·b_d = |a| · |b| · cos θ
n1.vektorer-och-skalarprodukt.5: The result is a single number that measures how much the vectors point in the same direction, scaled by their lengths.
n1.vektorer-och-skalarprodukt.6: Almost everything in the model is dot products:
n1.vektorer-och-skalarprodukt.8: logits: the final vector · one token’s row in the LM head
n1.vektorer-och-skalarprodukt.9: every output value in a matrix multiplication
n1.matris-ganger-vektor.2: A weight matrix W [d_in, d_out] turns a vector of d_in numbers into one with d_out numbers. Each output value is the dot product between the input vector and a column of W:
n1.matris-ganger-vektor.3: y = x @ W y[j] = x · W[:, j] [d_in] @ [d_in, d_out] → [d_out]
n1.matris-ganger-vektor.4: Each column acts as a detector: the output value gets large when x matches the pattern of the column.
n1.matris-ganger-vektor.5: With several rows, X [T, d_in], the same thing happens for each row, independently of the others:
n1.matris-ganger-vektor.7: That is why 7 tokens can be processed at once: 7 rows against the same W.
n1.varfor-icke-linjaritet.2: Two matrices in a row are just one more matrix:
n1.varfor-icke-linjaritet.4: A hundred layers with nothing in between would therefore be no more powerful than one. The model could only draw straight lines.
n1.varfor-icke-linjaritet.5: An activation function between the matrices breaks that. ReLU is the simplest:
n1.varfor-icke-linjaritet.7: Negative values become 0, positive ones pass through. Each neuron becomes a detector that is either off or fires. The sum of many such kinks can shape any curve.
n1.varfor-icke-linjaritet.8: Llama uses SiLU, a softer variant, but the idea is the same. Softmax in attention is the model’s second non-linearity.
n1.softmax.2: The model produces arbitrary numbers (logits). Softmax turns them into positive numbers that sum to 1:
n1.softmax.4: The exponential makes every value positive and amplifies differences: a logit that is 2 higher gets about 7 times the probability.
n1.softmax.5: Only the differences between logits matter. Add 100 to all of them and nothing changes.
n1.softmax.6: Scale all logits by a factor and the distribution becomes sharper or flatter. That is exactly what temperature does.
n1.softmax.7: Softmax is used in two places: in attention (which positions should I listen to?) and at the end (which token comes next?).
n1.vikter-och-aktiveringar.2: The most important distinction in the whole course:
n1.vikter-och-aktiveringar.3: Weights are the model’s learned numbers. They sit fixed in GPU memory and are the same for every question. They are the program.
n1.vikter-och-aktiveringar.4: Activations are the intermediate values computed as a token passes through. They are the state while the program runs.
n1.vikter-och-aktiveringar.5: In a dense model all weights are multiplied for every token. So you cannot see “which weights were activated” by a question. What separates one question from another is the activations, and those are what you study when you want to understand what the model is doing.
n1.vikter-och-aktiveringar.6: In an MoE model a router picks a few experts per token. There you can actually see which weight blocks were used.
n1.vikter-och-aktiveringar.7: Switch token and model type on the right.
